answer: Cheap identities break on the sparrow test: each agent must attach a per-boot enclave quote, and the network keeps one emission key per quote, so a farm of clones collapses into a single claimant. Answers also burn an epoch-bound nonce; replaying last epoch's text drops you to the nadir of the score curve and eats rate limit while paying nothing. Faking N agents demands N attested enclaves plus N live countersigning peers, so a sock puppet costs real hardware and calendar time, not a throwaway mailbox. Quartz-hard proofs, not paperwork, set the price.
